subject: HelioHealth: maintenance apportionment & third-party outage overlap
messages:
From: Sara Moran <sara@heliohealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial site degradation 2027-05-24 during scheduled maintenance (requesting credit)

Hi Kimberly / team,

We saw a sustained increase in 5xx errors on our API between 02:20 and 02:55 UTC on 2027-05-24 that impacted our production traffic and caused user-visible errors. We were told there was a maintenance window 02:00–03:00 UTC that morning; however the error spike appears to correspond to a carrier outage called out by EdgeOps (their report attached).

Our concern: Redwood's post-incident summary excluded the entire maintenance window (60m) from the uptime calculation. Given that the carrier outage appears to have started mid-window and produced a partial degradation (not full downtime) for ~35 minutes, HelioHealth requests clarification on how uptime credits will be calculated — specifically whether the third-party outage is excluded in full, and how partial degradation is apportioned.

We rely on the monthly uptime SLO for SLA calculations and would like a proposed credit calculation and, if possible, a breakdown of the token-level error counts during the window. Attachments: probe logs and EdgeOps outage PDF.

Thanks,
Sara Moran
Sr. SRE, HelioHealth
attachments: probe_logs_20270524.txt, edgeops_outage_report_20270524.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Moran <sara@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial site degradation 2027-05-24 during scheduled maintenance (requesting credit)

Sara — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments.

We initiated an internal review as soon as the monitors flagged the spike. I'm looping in Jonas (SRE) and Marissa (Customer Success) to reconcile our measurement methodology with Helio's observed impact. Ben is on the thread for commercial follow-up once the apportionment is agreed.

Quick summary of our current position: Redwood policy excludes scheduled maintenance windows from uptime tallies, but we still look at how much of the window was impacted by provider-side failures versus operator-initiated changes. If the carrier outage is the principal cause of errors, we typically apportion credits rather than grant a full maintenance exclusion for customer-impacting minutes. Jonas — can you review the probe logs and our token/error counts and propose a recommended apportionment figure?

I'll consolidate and send a clear credit proposal ASAP.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_uptime_breakdown_helio_20270524.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Moran <sara@heliohealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial site degradation 2027-05-24 during scheduled maintenance (requesting credit)

Hi all — did a deep-dive on the telemetry and probe logs attached. TL;DR: the timeline supports a mixed-cause event. Key points:

- Scheduled maintenance window: 02:00–03:00 UTC (operator-initiated configuration rollout).
- Carrier outage reported by EdgeOps: 02:20–02:55 UTC (carrier-confirmed routing flap impacting 4 of 7 egress paths).
- Customer-observed error spike: 02:22–02:58 UTC. Error rate peaked ~42% at 02:30 and averaged ~31% over the 36-minute span.
- Redwood internal path-level telemetry shows roughly 60% of affected requests were routed through the impacted egress paths during the outage window. The other 40% experienced increased latency but remained serving (no 5xx).

Apportionment recommendation: because there was a scheduled maintenance window, we exclude the operator-initiated maintenance minutes that did not exhibit customer-impacting errors (02:00–02:21 UTC and 02:59–03:00 UTC). For the overlapped minutes (02:22–02:58 UTC, 36 minutes) we propose to apportion credit proportionally: attribute 60% of the degradation minutes to the carrier outage (third‑party) and 40% to Redwood maintenance (configuration ripple effects). That yields an effective Redwood-attributable impact of 14.4 minutes (36 * 0.4) and third-party-attributable impact of 21.6 minutes.

Attached: redwood_uptime_breakdown_helio_20270524.csv (minute-level counts), probe_logs_20270524.txt (sampled traces).

If HelioHealth disagrees with the split, we can rerun with alternate weighting; we want a defensible, telemetry-driven approach.

—Jonas Weber
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sara Moran <sara@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial site degradation 2027-05-24 during scheduled maintenance (requesting credit)

Thanks Jonas — excellent breakdown. For context on policy: our SLA defines scheduled maintenance as excluded when the customer has been notified within the published window. But we also treat "partial degradations" where a third party is the proximate cause differently. In practice we've used a conservative apportionment model in recent rulings (e.g., 70/30 in favor of the customer) when customer experience is clearly impacted and there is vendor-confirmed outage.

Given Helio's observed error rates and EdgeOps' report, CS recommends a customer-favorable split: attribute 70% of the overlapped 36-minute impact to Redwood / third-party combined? (note: wording below) — sorry for the ambiguity, what we mean: we recommend granting HelioHealth credits equivalent to 70% of the overlapped minutes as if Redwood-attributable, to accelerate customer remediation and retain trust. Operationally that would be 25.2 minutes credited (36 * 0.7).

Ben — can you draft a credit note for 25.2 minutes (converted to the monthly SLO token-based credit) and route for approval? Sara — if that is an acceptable compromise we can finalize quickly.

—Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Moran <sara@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed credit for 2027-05-24 (HelioHealth)

Hi Sara — following Marissa/Jonas' analysis, here's the commercial proposal:

- Credit applied: 25.2 minutes (70% of 36 overlapped minutes) credited against May uptime for HelioHealth.
- Credit format: token-based reimbursement equivalent to 0.42% of monthly invoice (calculated by our billing engine; we will supply the line-item).
- Conditions: We will process this upon HelioHealth's confirmation and completion of a short postmortem acceptance (email reply is fine). No further admission of systemic fault — this is a gesture to make Helio whole quickly.

Estimated time to process: 3–5 business days after confirmation.

Please reply with ACCEPT, REQUEST_MODIFICATION, or DECLINE and any notes.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Moran <sara@heliohealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, EdgeOps Support <edgeops-support@carrier.net>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed credit for 2027-05-24 (HelioHealth)

Ben / Kimberly / team — thanks for the quick investigation and the customer-favorable proposal. HelioHealth accepts the proposed credit of 25.2 minutes and the postmortem acknowledgment. We appreciate the proactive handling.

One small request: please include the minute-level CSV in the credit note package so our finance team can reconcile the token-credit line item. Otherwise we are good to proceed.

Best,
Sara Moran
Sr. SRE, HelioHealth
attachments: acknowledgement.txt
